answer: Sybil resistance comes from giving each identity its own non-transferable stake. An agent must lock a fixed minimum deposit from its own spendable balance to register. Since the deposit is per identity and never pooled, spawning N agents costs N times that minimum at once, with no discount. Slashing is automatic: if a cluster votes alike, shares a funding trail, or fails liveness, the whole deposit burns. The attacker pays upfront for every voice and risks it all on one detection, so cost outpaces reward. Each fake account is a karst sink, a comet that burns out unpaid, a thread.
